workflow_steps.objective: Define the product goals, learner audience, curriculum scope, platforms, constraints, supplied materials, success criteria and unresolved decisions.
Study learner needs, educator and caregiver contexts, comparable products, accessibility requirements and age-appropriate AI-learning conventions.
Establish learning, interaction, visual, character, accessibility and responsible-AI principles that govern the system.
Map lesson hierarchy, screen states, content types and reusable module anatomy from learning objective through instruction, practice, feedback and completion.
Translate the learning principles and curriculum goals into repeatable exercise, prompting, feedback and reflection patterns.
Define a scalable workflow connecting curriculum inputs to lesson modules, interaction specifications, character and graphic assets, review, testing and final screens.
Develop meaningfully different visual, character and interaction directions demonstrated across representative lesson modules rather than isolated screens.
Compare directions against learning, usability, accessibility, scalability and brand criteria and obtain an explicit stakeholder choice.
Create a rough interactive lesson flow using the selected direction and test comprehension, engagement, navigation, feedback and AI-related expectations with representative users.
Apply validated feedback to the selected direction, lesson patterns and interactions while preserving approved system decisions.
Codify typography, colour, illustration, character behavior, iconography, motion, layout, component states and governance rules.
Apply the approved system across reusable content modules, character poses, graphic assets, interaction states and representative final learning screens.

missing_inputs: Target learner age ranges, developmental needs and reading levels
Curriculum subjects, learning standards and measurable outcomes
Representative lesson content and expected lesson duration
Definition of the AI functionality, its role in learning and required human oversight
Existing brand identity, product design system and reusable assets
Supported devices, platforms, orientations and technical constraints
Child privacy, safeguarding, moderation, consent and legal requirements
Character roles, tone, representation requirements and asset-volume expectations
Primary user contexts, including educator, caregiver and independent-child use
Research access, testing participants and success metrics
Stakeholder approval roles, schedule, budget and final handoff specifications
assumptions: The product is a screen-based interactive learning experience, but its exact platform is not yet known.
The system should support multiple lessons and content topics through reusable rules and modules.
Learning efficacy, comprehension, accessibility and child safety will be evaluated alongside visual appeal and engagement.
Character and graphic assets will be governed as reusable families with defined roles, states and behaviors.
Representative lesson flows will be approved before the system is expanded across the full content library.
Qualified curriculum, accessibility, privacy and child-safety reviewers will participate in approval.
No existing brand or product system is assumed because none was supplied.
stop_conditions: Do not begin concept exploration until the learner audience, curriculum scope, AI role and representative lesson content are defined.
Do not select a direction without an explicit human stakeholder decision against agreed learning, accessibility and scalability criteria.
Do not expand the system across the content library until a representative interactive lesson has been prototyped and evaluated with appropriate users or expert proxies.
Stop if proposed AI interactions cannot satisfy applicable child-safety, privacy, consent, moderation or human-oversight requirements.
Do not finalize character or graphic families until representation, tone, usage rights and required asset states are approved.
Do not deliver production-ready assets until platform specifications, accessibility acceptance criteria, content ownership and handoff requirements are confirmed.
rationale: The sequence establishes educational and responsible-AI foundations first, converts them into lesson architecture and reusable activities, defines the operating model that links content to production, and then validates a selected visual and interaction direction before systematizing and expanding it. This keeps final screens, characters and graphics traceable to shared learning and design rules rather than treating them as isolated illustrations.
